text: Shah Faesal, born on 17 May 1983 in the Sogam area of Lolab Valley, Kupwara district, Jammu and Kashmir, is an Indian bureaucrat currently serving as Deputy Secretary in the Ministry of Culture (India) and previously in the Union Ministry for Tourism. His father, Ghulam Rasool Shah, was a teacher killed by militants in 2002 when Faesal was 19; his mother, Mubeena Shah, and grandfather were also teachers. Faesal graduated in 2008 from Jhelum Valley Medical College and earned an MBBS from Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS), Srinagar, completing his medical degree at age 26. He holds a master's degree in Urdu and was a gold medalist at SKIMS during his medical studies. In 2009, he secured Rank 1 in the UPSC civil services examination, becoming the first Kashmiri to top it and the first from Kashmir in several years to be selected to the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) through open merit. He was also the fourth Muslim (after Independence) to achieve this rank. Faesal was appointed assistant commissioner, revenue, of Pulwama district on 16 August 2012, transferred to deputy commissioner of Bandipora on 8 February 2014, and later served as Director School Education, Kashmir, from 22 August 2015 until 18 October 2016, when Ajaz Ahmad Bhat took over. He was temporarily given additional charge of the vice-chairman of J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority on 26 March 2016. In May 2018, he was transferred to the J&K State Power Development Corporation as managing director, later asked to remain in his post, and received the Fulbright-Nehru Masters' Fellowship in May 2018 to study at the Harvard Kennedy School. On 9 January 2019, he tendered his resignation from the IAS via a Facebook post, citing "unabated killings" in Kashmir and disillusionment with his role, including jailing people and imposing curfews, which the central government reportedly rejected and he later withdrew. On 4 February 2019, he began his political life with a public speech in Kupwara, where he compared his IAS experience to spending 10 years in jail. On 25 February 2019, he announced during a live NDTV debate that he was launching a political party and had applied to the Election Commission. On 16 March 2019, he announced the formation of the Jammu and Kashmir People's Movement (JKPM) on 17 March at a football ground in Rajbagh, Srinagar, stating it would provide a platform for youth and veteran politicians with a clean image. The party did not contest the 2019 Indian general election and focused on outreach, emphasizing the protection of Article 370 and Article 35A of the Indian Constitution. On 18 June 2019, he and Engineer Rashid announced a political alliance called the Peoples United Front with the Awami Ittehad Party, advocating for the resolution of the Kashmir dispute based on Kashmiri wishes, peaceful India-Pakistan relations, protection of the state's special status, return of Kashmiri Pandits, and release of detained politicians. Faesal was detained on 14 August 2019 while attempting to fly to Turkey, taken into preventive detention first at the Centaur Hotel and later at the MLA hostel, where he remained for six months. He filed a habeas corpus plea in the Delhi High Court in August 2019, claiming he was going to the U.S. for studies and had been illegally detained; the government argued he lacked a student visa and had provoked protests, and claimed he refused to guarantee he would not repeat such actions. The plea was withdrawn by his wife in September 2019. He was booked under the Public Safety Act (PSA) in February 2020, accused of subtly advocating separatism, with the detention extended by three months on 13 May, and revoked on 3 June 2020, after a 10-month detention, followed by immediate house arrest. He was reinstated in the Indian Administrative Service in April 2022 and posted as Deputy Secretary in the Union Ministry for Tourism in August 2022. On 10 August 2020, JKPM announced that Faesal had decided to exit politics and requested to be relieved from the party, which complied, with Chairman Javaid Mustafa Mir appointed as his replacement. Faesal has written for the Greater Kashmir newspaper and participated in the Jammu & Kashmir Right to Information movement with Dr. Raja Muzaffar Bhat. He made bold social media posts, including a tweet in July 2018 stating "Population +patriarchy +illiteracy +alcohol +porn +technology +anarchy = rapistan," which he clarified was not about India, though disciplinary action was taken by both the J&K and central governments. During the 2016 Kashmir unrest, he urged national media not to use his image in comparison with Burhan Wani, threatening to resign if such comparisons continued. In 2019, Hizbul Mujahideen circulated a poster warning about Faesal. In February 2019, the Ministry of Home Affairs withdrew security cover from 155 people in Jammu and Kashmir, including Faesal. On 14 August 2019, he was stopped at IGI Airport while attempting to travel to Turkey and returned to Kashmir. He has named both Prime Minister Imran Khan and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal as role models. Mani Shankar Aiyar wrote an article titled "Kashmir's Arvind Kejriwal" about Faesal. On 3 March 2019, he recommended the Nobel Peace Prize for Imran Khan for "saving South Asia from a nuclear catastrophe." During a talk at the India International Center in February 2019, he described Kashmir as a "High Altitude Graveyard," advocating for "humanising the discourse" and urging people not to view the Kashmir issue as merely a "law and order problem." On 5 March 2021, he tweeted, "Friends let’s sort it out for once. I have always been pro-India. But now I am single-mindedly, shamelessly, helplessly and unapologetically pro-India. I stick to my side. It is a long story and I have to tell this story one day. But this is how it is going to be. Peace." Shah Faesal is married to Iram Rashid, an officer of the KAS, and has a son named Jami Faesal.
